evidence.restatement: Holi, the Hindu festival of colours held in spring (Phalguna), is famous for throwing coloured powder and water.
Pongal (a Tamil harvest festival in January), Onam (a Kerala harvest festival) and Navratri (nine nights honouring Durga) are not colour-throwing festivals.
On the eve of Holi, Holika Dahan bonfires recall Holika burning in the fire while the devotee Prahlad was saved.
Holi powders (gulal, abir) were traditionally made from natural plant sources such as palash (tesu) flowers and herbs, before synthetic dyes.
Holi, a Hindu spring festival, is famous for people throwing coloured powder and water.
Navratri is nine nights of worship and dance, Pongal a Tamil harvest festival in January and Onam a Kerala harvest festival; none involves throwing colour.
Bonfires on the eve of Holi (Holika Dahan) recall Holika, who burned while the devotee Prahlad came to no harm.
Gulal is the traditional Holi powder, historically made from flowers such as palash and herbs such as turmeric and neem.
